title: SSE graceful gap-recovery, chunk-lineage, and ordered tool-call interop
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a production-grade SSE streaming mode that tolerates short connection gaps without losing function-call ordering or structured-output lineage. This ticket defines a compact chunk-lineage header, gap-recovery semantics, and an ordered tool-call reconciliation strategy compatible with existing JSONL and EventStream clients.

Background: Current SSE behavior retries by re-establishing streams and sending resume tokens or replays, but in high-latency mobile and intermittent-network scenarios we see partial tool-call duplication or out-of-order tool invocations after reconnect. This causes customer-visible duplicate side effects (duplicate callbacks, duplicate DB writes) or dropped structured outputs when clients drop fragments. Previous tickets addressed framing but did not provide a minimal lineage and reconciliation policy that spans both streaming text chunks and function/tool call frames.

Goal: Provide an interoperable protocol extension and server-side behavior that: 1) preserves chronological ordering of tool-call events across reconnects; 2) enables clients to detect and request missing chunks by sequence watermarks; 3) includes a compact chunk-lineage envelope that allows idempotent reapplication of tool outputs or safe deduplication on the consumer side. The changes must be backward-compatible for clients that do not implement the extension, and opt-in via headers or connection negotiation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Server emits chunk-lineage metadata (sequence id, segment id, parent-checksum, partial-offset) in each SSE data payload header for negotiated clients.
- On reconnect, client can request 'gap-recovery' by sending last-ack-seq and optional client-window; server will replay missing chunks for up to the configured retention window (default 30s) or fallback to canonical fallback-model response when replay is unavailable.
- Function/tool-call frames include stable call-id and call-seq; server guarantees at-least-once delivery but provides reconciliation hints so clients can dedupe or request exact replays.
- End-to-end test harness demonstrates: (a) simulated mid-stream TCP drop with replay succeeds without duplicate tool-execution when client follows dedupe hints; (b) clients lacking negotiation continue to receive legacy SSE with no behavioral changes.
- API docs and migration guide published in Console docs and examples for Node/python SDKs.
- Feature gated behind runtime flag and rolloutable per-customer (Dedicated/Private) in console.
implementation_notes: Connection negotiation: add optional header X-Redwood-Stream-Mode: lineage-v1 during SSE handshake. If absent, server falls back to legacy streaming path.

Chunk-lineage envelope: inline small metadata JSON at start of SSE data block separated by a fixed sentinel '
' to remain friendly to existing JSONL consumers. Fields: seq (int), seg (int), parent_sha1 (hex), fragment_offset (int), call_id (uuid optional). Keep envelope <=256 bytes.

Server-side retention: keep per-stream sliding buffer of last N seconds (configurable, default 30s) keyed by customer and connection id to support gap replays. Ensure memory bounds and LRU eviction by seq.

Tool-call ordering: attach stable call-seq per logical conversation. When replaying, include replay=true hint; clients must ignore duplicate call outcomes if they have observed call_id previously. Provide SDK helper util to dedupe by call_id in Node/Python.
Compatibility: legacy clients will ignore unknown header and see raw SSE text; implement dual-path streaming handlers to avoid regressions. Add integration tests with older SDK versions in CI matrix.
Telemetry: emit metrics for reconnect-rate, replay-hit-rate, duplicate-call-count, and avg-replay-latency. Tag by customer and model variant for troubleshooting.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flag behind runtime flag; enable for internal canary customers. 2) Add SDK support in Node/Python SDKs (minor version bump) and example migration guide. 3) Enable for small percentage of hosted traffic and observe metrics for duplicates/replays. 4) Ramp to 100% in 2 weeks if duplicate-call decreases and no regressions. 5) Enable as opt-in for Dedicated/Private via Console toggle.

Rollback: disable flag and fall back to legacy SSE stream. Ensure no persisted state required to disable.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for chunk-lineage envelope parser, sequence validation, and dedupe helper.
- Integration test: emulate server dropping connection at various offsets and verify client receives gap-replay and that tool calls are not double-applied when client consults call_id history.
- Load test: ensure retention buffer and replay path add <5% CPU latency at 1k req/s per GPU shard.
- Security: verify envelope cannot be abused for header injection and that parent_sha1 uses HMAC keyed by runtime secret for tamper-detection if enabled.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: high-memory growth for retention buffers during spike. Mitigation: strict per-customer caps, LRU eviction, and circuit-breaker to stop buffering when beyond threshold.
- Risk: SDK adoption lag leads to incorrect dedupe behavior. Mitigation: ship server-side conservative heuristics to mark replays and log duplicates while preserving at-least-once semantics until clients adopt SDK dedupe.
- Risk: tool-call side effects still possible if third-party webhooks are not idempotent. Mitigation: recommend webhook best-practices and provide token-based idempotency header for customers to validate.
